raw_response:
I farm only 18 mu, so I can’t push too hard on every crop. I have to keep some steady grain from wheat and maize, and I also keep some cash crops because vegetables and stevia can bring money if the year goes alright. I’ve farmed 10 years, and with my schooling I mostly go by what worked before and what people around me are doing. On the 8 mu that is in wheat-maize rotation, I will keep doing that because it is the safest. Wheat gives me grain and straw, then maize goes in right after harvest, same as most families here. I won’t cut fertilizer too much because if wheat turns yellow or maize stays short, the loss is bigger than saving a little cash.

For the other land, I’ll keep smaller vegetable area because cabbage and eggplant need more watching and more spray, but they bring cash faster. Stevia I will keep on a bigger piece because some neighbors had decent returns with it and it doesn’t need as much daily picking as vegetables. I have well water, so I can protect the crop if spring is dry, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate unless the soil is really drying or the crop is at an important stage.

I will not cut fertilizer too much on grain crops because once yield drops, it is hard to make that money back.
